items.text: The system shall support cruise discovery through a single search workflow that combines destination, departure port, departure month, and trip duration criteria.

claims.claim: A single cruise search workflow exposes controls for destination, departure port, dates, duration, and a search action.
The same workflow is progressively configured with Alaska, San Francisco, CA, June 2023, and 10+ days.

items.evidence_note: Step 9 shows all four configured criteria in the same search bar before submission.
items.rationale: The visible flow supports a single combined search workflow for the task criteria.

items.text: The system shall allow the user to select a cruise destination or region from a browseable set of sailing destinations.

claims.claim: The destination selector opens a browseable set of sailing destinations or regions.
A destination or region can be selected from that set, with Alaska shown as selected.

items.evidence_note: The open destination panel lists multiple regions and the selected option is marked.
items.rationale: The screenshots visibly support both browsing and selecting a cruise destination.

items.text: The system shall retain the selected destination in the search controls while the user configures the rest of the query.

claims.claim: After Alaska is selected, the destination remains visible in the Sail To control while later criteria are configured.

items.evidence_note: Alaska remains displayed across the later sail-from, date, and duration steps.
items.rationale: The selected destination is retained in the visible controls through the rest of the shown configuration flow.

items.text: The system shall allow the user to choose a sail-from location from a list of departure ports.
items.annotation_notes: The sail-from control expands into multiple departure locations and the flow selects San Francisco, CA.

claims.claim: The sail-from selector opens a list of departure ports.
The user can choose San Francisco, CA from the departure port list.

items.evidence_note: The port list includes several locations and San Francisco, CA is marked as selected.
items.rationale: The visible UI supports choosing a sail-from location from a departure-port list.

items.text: The system shall preserve the selected departure port while subsequent search criteria are edited.

claims.claim: After San Francisco, CA is selected, the departure port remains visible while later search criteria are edited.

items.evidence_note: San Francisco, CA remains displayed when date and duration controls are used later.
items.rationale: The visible sequence supports preservation of the selected departure port during subsequent configuration.

items.text: The system shall keep the selected sailing month and year visible as part of the active search query.

claims.claim: After June 2023 is selected, the selected month and year remain visible in the active Dates control.

items.evidence_note: The Dates control displays Jun 2023 after selection and while duration is configured.
items.rationale: The selected sailing month and year are visibly kept as part of the active query.

items.text: The system shall allow cruise searches to be filtered by duration bands such as 2 to 5 days, 6 to 9 days, and 10 plus days.

claims.claim: The duration selector exposes duration bands including 2-5 Days, 6-9 Days, and 10+ Days.
A duration band can be selected, with 10+ Days shown as selected.

items.evidence_note: The duration panel lists the stated bands and the final state marks 10+ Days as active.
items.rationale: The visible UI supports filtering by broad duration bands.

items.text: The system shall provide a search action that the user can invoke after configuring cruise criteria.
items.annotation_notes: A prominent Search Cruises action is visible throughout the flow and remains available after the query is configured.

claims.claim: A Search Cruises action is visible in the search workflow.
The Search Cruises action remains available after the destination, port, date, and duration are configured.

items.evidence_note: The red Search Cruises button is visible next to the configured controls.
items.rationale: The configured query has an available visible search action before submission.

items.text: The system shall keep the currently configured search criteria visible together before search execution so the user can review the query state.

claims.claim: Before search execution, the configured destination, departure port, date, and duration are visible together in the search controls.
The grouped visible criteria allow the user to review the query state before invoking search.

items.evidence_note: Step 9 shows Alaska, San Francisco, CA, Jun 2023, and 10+ Days together beside the search button.
items.rationale: The final pre-search state visibly supports review of the configured query.

items.text: The system shall provide clear visual feedback when a selector is configured on it's current state.
items.annotation_notes: Expanded selectors are visibly highlighted and chosen options are marked through active styling and check-state indicators.

claims.claim: Configured selectors display their current selected values in the search controls.
Selected options receive visible active-state feedback such as highlighting and check indicators.

items.evidence_note: Selected values appear in the controls and selected options are highlighted or marked with green checks.
items.rationale: The visible UI provides clear feedback about the current configured state of selectors.

items.text: The system shall allow the user to revise any individual search criterion before submitting the search.

claims.claim: Each individual search criterion remains visible as its own control before submission.
The controls retain dropdown affordances, indicating each criterion can be reopened or adjusted before search.

items.evidence_note: Step 9 shows separate Sail To, Sail From, Dates, and Duration controls with visible dropdown indicators before the search action.
items.rationale: The visible mechanism supports revising individual criteria before submitting, although no actual changed revision is performed in the flow.

items.text: The system shall return cruise results that reflect the combined selected destination, departure port, month, and duration after the search is submitted.

claims.claim: The visible query is configured with destination, departure port, month, and duration before submission.
Search results reflecting the combined selected criteria are shown after submission.
Whether returned cruises actually reflect all selected filters depends on result correctness not visible in the screenshots.

items.evidence_note: The flow stops before a search result page is shown.
items.rationale: The query configuration is visible, but the required result outcome is not visibly demonstrated.

items.text: The system shall allow users to select sailing dates at month and year granularity across multiple years.

claims.claim: The date selector presents months grouped by year.
The date selector shows selectable month options across multiple years.
A specific month and year can be selected, with June 2023 shown as selected.

items.evidence_note: The date panel is organized under 2023, 2024, and 2025 and June 2023 is selected.
items.rationale: The visible date selector supports month and year granularity across multiple years.

items.text: The system shall expose only genuinely searchable or available itinerary options for the user's query context when presenting destination, port, date, and duration choices.

claims.claim: The system presents itinerary options for destination, departure port, month, and duration choices.
The presented itinerary options are genuinely searchable or available for the user's query context.

items.evidence_note: The option lists are visible, but the screenshots do not expose inventory, availability, or searchability logic behind those options.
items.rationale: The core availability claim cannot be reliably judged from the visible screenshots alone.

items.text: The system shall preserve already selected cruise search criteria when the user leaves the search flow and returns later in the same browsing session.

claims.claim: Already selected cruise search criteria are preserved during the visible in-flow configuration sequence.
The selected criteria are preserved after leaving the search flow and returning later in the same browsing session.

items.evidence_note: The visible flow supports short-term in-flow retention but does not show leaving and returning to the search flow.
items.rationale: The requirement extends visible retention into session persistence, which is not demonstrated by the screenshots.

items.text: The system shall present search results only for sailings that are currently available under the combined selected destination, departure port, sailing month, and duration filters, and shall show user-facing feedback when no matching cruises are available.

claims.claim: The combined destination, departure port, sailing month, and duration filters can be configured before search.
Search results are limited to currently available sailings under the combined selected filters.
The system shows user-facing feedback when no matching cruises are available.

items.evidence_note: The combined search criteria are visible before submission, but no submitted results or no-results state is shown.
items.rationale: Filter setup is supported, while result availability correctness and no-match feedback are not verified.

items.text: The system shall return all cruises that satisfy the configured destination, departure port, sailing month, and duration criteria, without omitting any eligible sailings.

claims.claim: The configured cruise criteria are available before submission.
All eligible cruises satisfying the configured criteria are returned without omissions.

items.evidence_note: No results page, complete inventory reference, or post-search result set is shown.
items.rationale: The completeness of returned cruises cannot be judged from the screenshots.

items.text: The system shall provide the same cruise search criteria and equivalent search behavior to anonymous users and signed-in users unless a visible policy restriction is communicated.

claims.claim: Signed-in users have access to the cruise search criteria in the flow.
Anonymous users have the same cruise search criteria and equivalent search behavior.
A policy restriction is communicated when anonymous and signed-in search behavior differs.

items.evidence_note: The screenshots show a signed-in context with cruise search controls, but no anonymous comparison state or policy-restriction state is shown.
items.rationale: The comparative requirement cannot be reliably judged without an anonymous-user state.

items.text: The system shall provide a dedicated pre-search review step or summary panel that lists all selected cruise criteria together and allows the user to edit any one of them before submitting the search.

claims.claim: A dedicated pre-search review step or summary panel is provided before submitting the search.
The dedicated review step or summary panel lists all selected cruise criteria together.
The dedicated review step or summary panel allows editing of individual selected criteria before submission.
The selected cruise criteria are available together before submission.

items.evidence_note: The full visible pre-search sequence uses inline search controls. Step 9 shows all criteria together inline, but no separate review step or summary panel appears before the Search Cruises action.
items.rationale: The dedicated review-panel requirement is contradicted by the visible pre-search flow.

items.text: The system shall allow the user to filter cruises by an exact itinerary length in days in addition to broad duration bands.

claims.claim: The system supports broad duration-band filtering.
The system allows filtering by an exact itinerary length in days in addition to broad duration bands.

items.evidence_note: The visible duration choices are broad bands only: 2-5 Days, 6-9 Days, and 10+ Days. No exact day-length option is shown in the open duration choices.
items.rationale: The opened duration selector provides visible counter-evidence against exact-day filtering.
